question: The British acquisition of Zamindari rights over Sutanuti, Kalikata, and Gobindapur in 1698 was negotiated with Subahdar Azim-ush-Shan. Who was the chief English negotiator responsible for this transaction, and what was its legal character under Mughal law?
options: Job Charnock; it was a sovereign land grant exempt from all taxes
Charles Eyre; it was a lease transfer from the Sabarna Roy Choudhury family, making the Company a subject landlord (zamindar) under Mughal revenue law
William Hedges; it was an imperial farman direct from Aurangzeb bypassing the local Subahdar
John Surman; it was an outright purchase of sovereignty over the territory
explanation: In 1698, Charles Eyre (Job Charnock's son-in-law and EIC agent) negotiated the transfer of zamindari rights of the three villages from the Sabarna Roy Choudhury family of zamindars, with the permission of Azim-ush-Shan (the Subahdar of Bengal). The EIC paid Rs 1,200 to the family and became a Mughal zamindar, paying an annual land revenue (jama) of about Rs 1,195 to the Mughal state, remaining legal subjects of the empire.
